newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Most EU countries met EMU price goal in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Most EU countries met EMU price goal in Jan.

text.p: Eleven EU countries were in line with the inflation criterion for monetary union in January, according to harmonised price data measuring the moving average annual rates, a European Commission official said on Friday.

When comparing the average inflation of the year to end- January 1997 with the year to the end of the same month last year, only Greece, Spain, Portugal and Italy did not meet the price stability criterion, the official said.
The European Commission published on Friday harmonised inflation data measured both as changes year-on-year and as average annual inflation. These ways of measuring inflation show different rates.
When comparing January this year with the same month last year, only three countries -- Spain, Greece and Portugal -- did not make it.

The European Union executive has traditionally used the average rate of inflation, but it is still unclear exactly how the price stability criterion will be calculated when EU leaders decide in early 1998 which countries fulfill the requirement. The same harmonised method was used for both rates.
Here is a table of January harmonised inflation data for the 15 member states, measured both as year-on-year and as moving average rates.

NOTE - According to the EU's Maastricht Treaty, a country's average inflation rate observed over a year before joining EMU should "not exceed by more than 1.5 percentage points that of, at most, the three best performing member states in terms of price stability". -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
